title: Eternal decree to remit vs actual remission in time—do not confuse them
source_text: III. Porro Deus ab aeterno decrevit electis omnibus omnia omnino peccata remittere. Nec enim in tempore ulla gratia fruuntur, quae ipsis ab aeterno praeparata & destinata non sit. Sed multum distingui debet decretum de condonandis, sive remittendis electorum peccatis, ab actuali peccatorum illorum remissione & condonatione. Aliud est enim praestare ut electi definant reapse obnoxii esse poenis quas peccatum meretur, & aliud decretum formare de hoc ipso olim praestando. Sicut aliud est electum sanctificare, & aliud futuram ejus sanctificationem decernere. Deus autem non aliter electis peccata remittit, quam praestando ut cessent obnoxii esse poenis, ad quas peccatum eos obstringit.
pass_a_gloss: Further, God from eternity decreed to remit to all the elect absolutely all sins. For they enjoy in time no grace which was not prepared and destined for them from eternity. But the decree concerning pardoning, or remitting, the elect’s sins must carefully be distinguished from the actual remission and pardon of those sins. For it is one thing to bring it about that the elect actually cease to be liable to the penalties sin deserves, and another to form a decree about someday doing this. Just as it is one thing to sanctify an elect person, and another to decree his future sanctification. But God remits sins to the elect in no other way than by bringing it about that they cease to be liable to the penalties to which sin binds them.
pass_b_english: Eternal decree prepares every grace the elect will enjoy—including pardon.
Yet decree ≠ actual remission: God remits only by making them cease to be penalty-liable.
